text:
CrashLoopBackOff caused by missing or invalid ConfigMap/Secret
Scenario: crashloop
Symptoms: CrashLoopBackOff; CreateContainerConfigError; missing configuration; authentication failure at startup
Root causes: missing ConfigMap; missing Secret; wrong key name; invalid mounted content
CHECK [R] kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> :: find missing object/key events
CHECK [R] kubectl get configmap,secret -n <ns> :: confirm referenced object exists without exposing secret data
CHECK [R] kubectl get deployment/<name> -n <ns> -o yaml :: inspect references and key names
FIX [W] restore expected ConfigMap/Secret from approved source or correct reference :: approval=True
FIX [W] restart rollout after configuration is restored :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous object version from secret manager/config repository; roll back Deployment revision
Verify: pod starts; mount/env references resolve; application authentication succeeds
Safety: never place secret values in RAG, logs, prompts or audit output; compare names and hashes, not plaintext secret content

metadata.title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by missing or invalid ConfigMap/Secret
metadata.tags: CrashLoopBackOff CreateContainerConfigError ConfigMap Secret missing key
metadata.source: Blackout Ops curated runbook plus P0 case labels

text:
CrashLoopBackOff caused by unavailable dependency
Scenario: crashloop
Symptoms: CrashLoopBackOff; connection refused; timeout; dependency not ready
Root causes: database unavailable; upstream Service has no endpoints; startup ordering assumption; network policy block
CHECK [R] kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous :: identify dependency host, port and failure
CHECK [R] kubectl get svc,endpointslice -n <ns> :: confirm dependency service and ready endpoints
CHECK [R] kubectl get networkpolicy -A :: identify policy that may block traffic
FIX [W] restore dependency or correct endpoint/port configuration :: approval=True
FIX [W] add bounded retry/backoff or startup probe so transient dependency delay does not crash process :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous endpoint, environment variable or NetworkPolicy; roll back workload revision
Verify: dependency connection succeeds; pod Ready; restart count stable; end-to-end request succeeds
Safety: do not delete NetworkPolicy as a diagnostic shortcut; validate least-privilege connectivity

metadata.title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by unavailable dependency
metadata.tags: CrashLoopBackOff connection refused dependency EndpointSlice NetworkPolicy
metadata.source: Blackout Ops curated runbook plus P0 case labels

text:
CrashLoopBackOff caused by invalid command, args, or image
Scenario: crashloop
Symptoms: CrashLoopBackOff; executable file not found; permission denied; exit code 126 or 127
Root causes: invalid container command; bad args; wrong image tag; binary missing or not executable
CHECK [R] kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> -c <container> --previous :: capture startup error
CHECK [R] kubectl get pod <pod> -n <ns> -o yaml :: inspect resolved image, command and args
CHECK [R] kubectl rollout history deployment/<name> -n <ns> :: compare failing revision with last healthy revision
FIX [W] correct image, command or args in source manifest and apply reviewed change :: approval=True
FIX [W] roll back to last healthy Deployment revision for rapid recovery :: approval=True
Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <ns> --to-revision=<known-good>
Verify: rollout status succeeds; pod remains Ready; previous-log startup error absent; service health check passes
Safety: record current revision before change; never substitute an unverified mutable image tag

metadata.title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by invalid command, args, or image
metadata.tags: CrashLoopBackOff invalid command exit 126 exit 127 image args
metadata.source: Kubernetes pod debugging documentation; ITBench Scenario-105 pattern

text:
CrashLoopBackOff caused by OOMKilled or low memory limit
Scenario: crashloop
Symptoms: CrashLoopBackOff; OOMKilled; exit code 137; container restarts
Root causes: memory limit too low; memory leak; startup memory spike; node memory pressure
CHECK [R] kubectl get pod <pod> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[*].lastState.terminated}' :: confirm OOMKilled, exit code and time
CHECK [R] kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> -c <container> --previous :: read previous crashed container log
CHECK [R] kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> :: inspect limits, events and node pressure
CHECK [R] kubectl top pod <pod> -n <ns> --containers :: compare observed memory with request and limit when metrics are available
FIX [W] raise memory request/limit only after measured requirement and capacity check :: approval=True
FIX [W] roll back release when memory regression began with current revision :: approval=True
FIX [W] fix memory leak or reduce startup concurrency :: approval=True
Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <ns>; restore previous resource requests and limits
Verify: new pod Ready; restart count stops increasing; memory stays below limit; service error rate recovers
Safety: do not raise limits beyond node capacity; check blast radius before rollout

metadata.title: CrashLoopBackOff caused by OOMKilled or low memory limit
metadata.tags: CrashLoopBackOff OOMKilled exit 137 memory limit pod failure
metadata.source: Kubernetes pod debugging documentation plus P0 case labels

text:
Container restart caused by liveness or startup probe misconfiguration
Scenario: crashloop
Symptoms: repeated restarts; Liveness probe failed; Startup probe failed; healthy process killed during warm-up
Root causes: wrong probe port; wrong protocol or path; initial delay too short; timeout too strict
CHECK [R] kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> :: confirm probe failure events
CHECK [R] kubectl get deployment/<name> -n <ns> -o yaml :: inspect probe protocol, port, path and timing
CHECK [R] kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous :: separate probe kill from application crash
FIX [W] correct probe endpoint/port/protocol :: approval=True
FIX [W] add startupProbe or tune timing from measured startup behavior :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous probe definition; kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <ns>
Verify: probe succeeds; pod Ready; restart count stable; application endpoint independently healthy
Safety: do not remove health probes permanently; avoid masking real application failure with excessive thresholds

metadata.title: Container restart caused by liveness or startup probe misconfiguration
metadata.tags: liveness probe startup probe readiness probe restart CrashLoopBackOff

text:
Cluster-wide DNS failure in CoreDNS
Scenario: dns
Symptoms: DNS fails across namespaces; kube-dns unavailable; SERVFAIL; CoreDNS errors
Root causes: CoreDNS pods unavailable; kube-dns Service missing; EndpointSlice empty; Corefile forwarding loop or bad upstream
CHECK [R] kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns :: check DNS pod health
CHECK [R] kubectl get svc kube-dns -n kube-system :: confirm DNS Service and ClusterIP
CHECK [R] kubectl get endpointslice -n kube-system -l kubernetes.io/service-name=kube-dns :: confirm ready DNS endpoints
CHECK [R] kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns :: inspect query and forwarding errors
FIX [W] restore reviewed CoreDNS ConfigMap/Corefile or upstream resolver :: approval=True
FIX [W] restart CoreDNS Deployment after configuration correction :: approval=True

text:
Service resolves but has no ready endpoints
Scenario: dns
Symptoms: DNS lookup succeeds; connection refused or timeout; EndpointSlice has no endpoints; Service unavailable
Root causes: Service selector mismatch; pods not Ready; targetPort mismatch; wrong protocol
CHECK [R] kubectl get svc <service> -n <ns> -o yaml :: inspect selector, port and targetPort
CHECK [R] kubectl get endpointslice -n <ns> -l kubernetes.io/service-name=<service> -o yaml :: inspect endpoint readiness and ports
CHECK [R] kubectl get pods -n <ns> --show-labels :: compare pod labels with Service selector
FIX [W] correct Service selector, port, targetPort or protocol :: approval=True
FIX [W] repair backing pod readiness failure when selector is correct :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous Service manifest; roll back backing workload revision
Verify: EndpointSlice contains ready endpoint; connection succeeds; end-to-end health check passes
Safety: distinguish DNS resolution from Service routing; preview selector matches before applying

text:
Kubernetes DNS failure from wrong Service name or namespace
Scenario: dns
Symptoms: no such host; NXDOMAIN; temporary failure in name resolution; short name works only in one namespace
Root causes: wrong Service name; wrong namespace; incorrect cluster domain; stale environment variable
CHECK [R] kubectl exec <debug-pod> -n <ns> -- nslookup <service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local :: test fully qualified service name from affected namespace
CHECK [R] kubectl get svc -A :: confirm exact Service name and namespace
CHECK [R] kubectl exec <pod> -n <ns> -- cat /etc/resolv.conf :: inspect search domains and nameserver
FIX [W] correct Service FQDN, namespace or application environment variable :: approval=True
FIX [W] roll out corrected workload configuration :: approval=True
Rollback: restore prior environment/config value; roll back Deployment revision
Verify: FQDN lookup returns ClusterIP; application connection succeeds; DNS error rate returns to baseline
Safety: verify from affected namespace; do not change cluster-wide DNS before proving cluster-wide impact

metadata.tags: DNS NXDOMAIN no such host Service namespace FQDN

text:
Pod startup failure from image registry DNS resolution
Scenario: dns
Symptoms: ImagePullBackOff; ErrImagePull; registry lookup failed; no such host
Root causes: node resolver cannot resolve registry; registry hostname incorrect; proxy or egress DNS path broken
CHECK [R] kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> :: capture exact image pull and DNS event
CHECK [R] nslookup <registry-host> :: test registry DNS from affected node context
CHECK [R] cat /etc/resolv.conf :: inspect affected node resolver configuration
FIX [W] correct registry hostname or node resolver/upstream DNS configuration :: approval=True
FIX [W] retry rollout after DNS path is restored :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous node resolver configuration; restore prior working image reference
Verify: registry hostname resolves; image pull succeeds; pod reaches Ready
Safety: do not bypass TLS or switch to an untrusted registry; do not expose registry credentials in diagnostics

text:
Kubernetes node DiskPressure
Scenario: disk_full
Symptoms: DiskPressure=True; node.kubernetes.io/disk-pressure taint; pod eviction; image filesystem full
Root causes: nodefs exhausted; imagefs exhausted; containerfs exhausted; inode exhaustion
CHECK [R] kubectl describe node <node> :: confirm DiskPressure condition, taint, capacity and eviction events
CHECK [R] kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp :: locate eviction and garbage-collection evidence
CHECK [R] crictl images && crictl ps -a :: inspect runtime images and stopped containers on affected node
CHECK [R] df -hT && df -i :: identify nodefs/imagefs/containerfs or inode pressure
FIX [W] allow kubelet garbage collection to reclaim dead containers and unused images; correct kubelet GC thresholds if misconfigured :: approval=True
FIX [W] fix workload ephemeral-storage requests/limits or runaway log source :: approval=True
FIX [D] manually remove only confirmed unused runtime artifacts when kubelet cannot recover :: approval=True
Rollback: restore prior kubelet configuration; roll back workload resource configuration
Verify: DiskPressure=False; disk-pressure taint cleared by controller; pods schedule normally; free space remains above threshold
Safety: do not use external garbage collection that can conflict with kubelet; do not manually remove active container layers

text:
Linux service connection refused or expected port not listening
Scenario: other
Symptoms: Connection refused; port not listening; upstream connect error; service unavailable on expected socket
Root causes: service stopped; process bound wrong address; wrong port configuration; startup failure; firewall rejection
CHECK [R] ss -lntup :: identify listening address, port and owning process
CHECK [R] systemctl status <unit> --no-pager -l :: inspect service state and exit status
CHECK [R] journalctl -u <unit> --since '-15 min' --no-pager :: capture bind or startup error
CHECK [R] curl -v --connect-timeout 3 http://<host>:<port>/<health-path> :: test exact address and port from approved network context
FIX [W] correct reviewed bind address or port configuration and restart only affected service :: approval=True
FIX [D] change firewall policy only after listener and path are proven healthy and the required flow is approved :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous service configuration; restore prior firewall policy; restart known-good unit configuration
Verify: ss shows expected listener; local and approved remote health checks pass; service error rate recovers
Safety: do not expose service on 0.0.0.0 without requirement; do not flush firewall rules; record affected interface and blast radius

metadata.tags: connection refused ss port listener bind systemd firewall

text:
Linux filesystem inode exhaustion
Scenario: disk_full
Symptoms: No space left despite free GiB; inode usage 100%; large number of tiny files
Root causes: runaway temporary files; unbounded cache; stale session or queue files
CHECK [R] df -i :: confirm inode exhaustion
CHECK [R] find <approved-path> -xdev -type f -printf '.' | wc -c :: count files only inside approved path
CHECK [R] find <approved-path> -xdev -type f -mtime +<days> -print :: preview stale deletion candidates
FIX [D] delete only previewed stale files covered by retention policy :: approval=True
FIX [W] add bounded retention or queue consumer fix :: approval=True
Rollback: restore deleted files from snapshot/backup when required; restore previous retention configuration
Verify: inode availability recovered; file creation succeeds; producer and consumer rates stable
Safety: approved-path must be explicit; no recursive delete against root, home, workspace, or unresolved variable

metadata.title: Linux filesystem inode exhaustion
metadata.tags: disk inode tiny files ENOSPC retention

text:
Linux disk full caused by logs or journal growth
Scenario: disk_full
Symptoms: No space left on device; filesystem usage near 100%; logs growing rapidly
Root causes: unbounded application logs; systemd journal retention too large; log rotation failed
CHECK [R] df -hT && df -i :: separate block exhaustion from inode exhaustion
CHECK [R] du -x -d 2 /var 2>/dev/null | sort -n | tail :: locate large directories without crossing filesystems
CHECK [R] journalctl --disk-usage :: measure journal usage
CHECK [R] lsof +L1 :: find deleted files still held open
FIX [W] fix logrotate policy, then rotate affected application logs :: approval=True
FIX [W] journalctl --rotate followed by approved --vacuum-size or --vacuum-time limit :: approval=True
FIX [W] restart only process holding a confirmed deleted large file :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous logrotate configuration; restart affected logger/application if rotation handoff fails
Verify: df usage below recovery threshold; application health check passes; log growth rate returns to baseline
Safety: never delete unknown files by size alone; journal vacuum removes archived journals only; record reclaimed bytes and affected service

metadata.title: Linux disk full caused by logs or journal growth
metadata.tags: disk filesystem journalctl logrotate no space left inode
metadata.source: Blackout Ops curated runbook; systemd journalctl official behavior

text:
Linux host DNS resolver failure
Scenario: dns
Symptoms: Temporary failure in name resolution; Name or service not known; SERVFAIL; NXDOMAIN; no such host
Root causes: wrong resolv.conf; systemd-resolved unavailable; bad upstream resolver; search-domain error; firewall blocks DNS
CHECK [R] getent ahosts <hostname> :: test resolution through libc/NSS used by applications
CHECK [R] resolvectl status && resolvectl query <hostname> :: inspect link-specific DNS and query result when systemd-resolved is used
CHECK [R] readlink -f /etc/resolv.conf && cat /etc/resolv.conf :: inspect resolver ownership, nameservers and search domains
CHECK [R] dig +time=2 +tries=1 <hostname> :: separate DNS protocol failure from application behavior
FIX [W] restore reviewed NetworkManager or systemd-resolved DNS configuration :: approval=True
FIX [W] restart the active resolver service after configuration validation :: approval=True
FIX [D] change firewall or routing rules only after proving DNS packets are blocked :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous resolver configuration; restore previous firewall rule set; restart prior resolver service configuration
Verify: getent and resolvectl resolve expected address; application lookup succeeds; unrelated internal names still resolve
Safety: do not overwrite a managed resolv.conf symlink blindly; test internal and external zones separately; preserve air-gapped resolver policy

metadata.title: Linux host DNS resolver failure
metadata.tags: DNS systemd-resolved resolv.conf getent SERVFAIL NXDOMAIN Temporary failure in name resolution

text:
Linux process killed by kernel or systemd OOM policy
Scenario: crashloop
Symptoms: Killed process; Out of memory; oom-kill; exit code 137; service restarts under memory load
Root causes: host memory exhaustion; cgroup MemoryMax too low; application memory leak; unbounded workload concurrency
CHECK [R] journalctl -k -g 'Out of memory|Killed process|oom-kill' --since '-30 min' --no-pager :: confirm kernel OOM victim and timestamp
CHECK [R] systemctl show <unit> -p MemoryCurrent -p MemoryMax -p MemoryHigh -p OOMPolicy :: inspect systemd cgroup memory policy
CHECK [R] cat /proc/meminfo && ps -eo pid,ppid,comm,rss,vsz --sort=-rss | head -20 :: measure host pressure and top consumers
FIX [W] fix application leak or bound concurrency; deploy reviewed change :: approval=True
FIX [W] adjust MemoryHigh or MemoryMax only after capacity and blast-radius checks :: approval=True
FIX [W] restart only the confirmed affected service after pressure is controlled :: approval=True
Rollback: restore prior systemd memory limits; roll back application revision
Verify: service remains active; memory stays below limit; no new OOM event; host available memory remains stable
Safety: do not disable memory controls globally; do not raise limits beyond physical capacity

metadata.title: Linux process killed by kernel or systemd OOM policy
metadata.tags: OOM oom-kill Killed process exit 137 MemoryMax cgroup systemd

text:
Linux systemd service restart loop or failed unit
Scenario: crashloop
Symptoms: service entered failed state; Start request repeated too quickly; restart counter increasing; process exits immediately
Root causes: invalid ExecStart; missing environment or file; permission failure; dependency unavailable; Restart policy loop
CHECK [R] systemctl status <unit> --no-pager -l :: capture unit state, exit status and recent messages
CHECK [R] journalctl -u <unit> --since '-15 min' --no-pager :: read complete failure sequence
CHECK [R] systemctl show <unit> -p FragmentPath -p ExecMainStatus -p NRestarts -p Restart :: inspect loaded unit, exit status and restart behavior
CHECK [R] systemd-analyze verify <unit-file> :: validate unit syntax without starting service
FIX [W] correct reviewed unit, environment, permissions or dependency configuration, then run systemctl daemon-reload :: approval=True
FIX [W] restart only the affected unit after configuration validation :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous unit or environment file; run systemctl daemon-reload; restart the known-good unit version
Verify: systemctl is-active returns active; NRestarts stops increasing; service health endpoint succeeds; journal has no new startup error
Safety: capture FragmentPath and current file before editing; do not disable Restart policy to hide an unresolved crash

metadata.title: Linux systemd service restart loop or failed unit
metadata.tags: systemd systemctl failed state restart loop Start request repeated too quickly journalctl

text:
Linux TLS service certificate expired or not yet valid
Scenario: other
Symptoms: x509 certificate has expired; certificate not yet valid; TLS handshake failed; certificate verify failed
Root causes: expired leaf certificate; expired intermediate certificate; wrong certificate deployed; host clock incorrect; renewal job failed
CHECK [R] date -u && timedatectl status :: rule out incorrect system time
CHECK [R] openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> -servername <host> -showcerts </dev/null :: capture served chain and verification result
CHECK [R] openssl x509 -in <certificate> -noout -subject -issuer -serial -dates :: inspect local certificate identity and validity
CHECK [R] systemctl list-timers --all | grep -Ei 'cert|acme|renew' :: inspect renewal scheduling without changing state
FIX [W] renew or restore the approved certificate chain through the configured CA/ACME workflow :: approval=True
FIX [W] validate service configuration, then reload only the affected TLS service :: approval=True
Rollback: restore previous certificate and key files from protected backup; reload the prior known-good service configuration
Verify: served certificate serial matches intended deployment; validity window includes current UTC time; TLS verification succeeds; service health check passes
Safety: never print or copy private keys into logs or prompts; do not disable TLS verification; treat certificate replacement as a scoped write action
